faq.q: What is the best app for dancers in 2026?
faq.a: It depends on the job. For learning classes, STEEZY. For recording and reviewing your own practice on iPhone or iPad, Dancify. For mirroring, slowing and looping a reference video, Dance.io. For coach-style video analysis, OnForm. For editing short videos, CapCut, Edits or iMovie. Most dancers use two or three of these together.

faq.q: What app can mirror and slow down dance videos?
faq.a: STEEZY can mirror, slow and loop its own classes. Dance.io mirrors, slows and loops any video you bring. YouTube slows videos to 0.25× and a browser extension such as Mirror Videos adds a mirror on a computer. Dancify mirrors, slows to 0.25× and loops your own takes.

Coach's Eye has been retired by TechSmith and is no longer a working service. For coach-style analysis with slow motion, drawing and side-by-side comparison, OnForm is a current alternative; for dance practice with a calendar of takes, loops and counts, Dancify is built for that job.
No. Hudl sold the Technique app to OnForm in May 2021, and Technique was discontinued later that year. Users were offered a migration tool to move their videos to OnForm.

faq.q: What is the best free app to record dance practice?
faq.a: The built-in Camera and Photos apps on iPhone are free and handle slow motion, trimming and flipping. Dancify's camera, practice diary and editor are free too, and add a musical count-in, Follow, loops and counts; only progress reels, side-by-side compare and the pose guide are Premium.

faq.q: Does Dancify have dance classes or tutorials?
faq.a: No. Dancify is a camera, practice diary and video editor for your own practice, not a class library. Many dancers learn on STEEZY or YouTube and then film and review their practice in Dancify, with the class video playing as a reference while they film. Dancify is available for iPhone and iPad only.
